You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.


New instance. Task id: task-9283d5f6
Test input (1x11):
2 2 1 8 6 6 2 2 1 2 2
Wrong attempts used: 0/8. Demo requests used: 0/8.
Reply with exactly one action JSON on the last line.

---
name: continual-arc
description: Solve Continual-ARC grid instances; follow the per-turn action protocol, infer transformations from demonstrations, and use feedback to choose the next action.
---

# Continual ARC

1. On every turn, emit exactly one valid protocol-action JSON object and nothing else; every feedback turn needs an action too. Check action fields, grid dimensions, and cell values before submitting.
2. Track wrong-attempt and demo budgets. Compare each demo input/output cellwise and seek a rule that explains all pairs. Check candidate line-based rules against every cell of each row or column; a changed complete line may be recolored throughout, not just at separator-colored cells. Do not generalize from partial alignment.
3. Before submitting, validate the rule on every demo, then apply it to the test while preserving cells outside predicted changes. If using code, verify output dimensions and all cells. Treat a demo request and wrong submission as equal-cost; request a demo only when it can distinguish live hypotheses.
4. After incorrect feedback, discard or materially revise the hypothesis by comparing the rejected output with every demo. Avoid unsupported variations; if uncertainty remains, request a discriminating demo within budget. (A symmetric/tiled-looking output is not sufficient evidence for a specific tiling or reflection rule; verify its mapping against the full demo before applying it.)
5. Stop only when the instance reports success/over or the attempt cap is reached; use `finish` only when allowed by the protocol.
